newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST-Akzo Nobel seen up strongly in Q4.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Akzo Nobel seen up strongly in Q4.

text.p: Dutch chemical group Akzo Nobel NV is seen posting solid profit growth in the 1996 fourth quarter, mainly reflecting better year-on-year performance in coatings and chemicals.

Analysts are forecasting fourth quarter net profit from ordinary operations of 273-320 million guilders, with consensus at 293 million guilders. In the year-earlier quarter Akzo posted ordinary net profit of 239 million guilders.
Full-year net profit is seen at 1.30-1.35 billion guilders versus 1.31 billion guilders in 1995.

"The 1995 fourth quarter was poor, particularly due to pressured margins in coatings and chemicals. I don't expect it to be as poor this quarter -- especially not in chemicals," said Robert Jan Stassen, analyst with Bangert Pontier and partners.
Coatings activities had finally started reaping the synergy benefits of the 1994 merger between Akzo and Nobel, structurally lifting margins by around one percent, he said.
ING Barings analyst Quirijn Mulder said operating results at chemicals would be driven higher by improved exchange rate conditions and increased volumes.
Chemicals accounted for some 34 percent of group sales during the first nine months of 1996.
"Chemicals are not completely over their problems yet," Mulder cautioned. "The whole PVC chain remains weak."
MeesPierson's Andreas de Groot agreed: "Chemicals will post a better result because of the poor 1995 fourth quarter, but underlying growth is not very good as yet."

Akzo's high-margin pharmaceuticals business was seen posting improved fourth-quarter results, partly because the thrombosis scare associated with its low-dosage contraceptive pill hit in the final 1995 quarter.
"Pharmaceuticals will edge up slightly, but the group result will lean mainly on chemicals and coatings," De Groot said.
The early marketing costs of Akzo's new fertility drug Puregon and anti-depressant Remeron would also likely brake earnings growth at pharmaceuticals, analysts said.
Akzo's fibres division was seen staying in the black after posting slender two million guilder operating profits in the third 1996 quarter, traditionally a difficult period.
"Fibres will turn in a reasonable performance," predicted ING's Mulder, while De Groot of MeesPierson said he expected fourth quarter operating profit of two million guilders.
Looking to 1997 and beyond, De Groot sees Akzo posting 7-10 percent profit growth this year. This could accelerate in 1998 as pharmaceuticals profits pick up on the back of new products.
"In terms of chemicals and coatings Akzo remains highly dependent on economic growth and we do not see this picking up in Europe before 1998," he said.
MeesPierson rates Akzo a "Hold", while Bangert and ING Barings both recommend the stock as a "Buy".
